key_insight: BI-RADS-grounded descriptors derived from breast MRI segmentation masks can guide an LLM to generate highly faithful lesion-assessment rationales.
clinical_relevance: This imaging-explainability approach—not drug discovery—could provide draft rationales for radiologist review and final sign-off.
method: Extract eight quantitative radiomic measurements, lesion size, and component count from masks and dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI.
Map measurements to descriptors through a BI-RADS-based decision tree.
Constrain an LLM to verbalize only the derived descriptor records.
evidence_signal: Across 1,506 MAMA-MIA cases, expert and automatic masks yielded 3,012 rationales with 99.98% faithfulness and 99.3% counterfactual accuracy.
watch_item: Descriptor agreement between expert and automatic masks declined from 0.832 for Good masks to 0.549 for Missed masks; faithful wording does not establish clinical correctness.
paper_title: Reading the Mask: Descriptor-Grounded BI-RADS Rationale Generation for Breast MRI Segmentation
